evidence.text: The *Shuowen* entry gives 想 as 冀思也 and analyzes it 从心，相聲, with fanqie 息兩切. This is the Han dictionary’s account of the graph, not independent proof of its earliest formation.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 說文資料搜索

evidence.text: Analyzes 想 as 心 semantic plus 相 phonetic and reports ‘thinking, pondering’ as its original sense. It cites the *Chu Ci* line 入景響之無應兮，聞省想而不可得, then lists imagining, hope/want, missing, conjecture, and ‘resemble’ uses. This is a lexicographic ordering, not a dated semantic chronology.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.field: 想; 字源字形與書證
evidence.text: The entry reports 春秋晚期 for a 想 inscription on 想簠, and displays a small-seal form under 說文 and an Eastern Han clerical form from the Kong Biao stele. These are reported identifications; the page does not provide an independently examined artifact catalogue or establish the bronze graph’s common-word sense.
evidence.title: 想 xiǎng - 漢典

evidence.text: Lists the transmitted *Chu Ci* example 入景響之無應兮，開省想而不可得 for thinking/pondering, and other citations for imagining, hope, missing, conjecture, and resemblance. These citations point to texts, not dated surviving graph witnesses; the list does not establish a first attestation or semantic chronology.
evidence.title: 想 xiǎng - 漢典

evidence.field: 想; 說文釋形與字樣說明
evidence.text: Gives both the Great Xu and Duan annotation versions of the *Shuowen* analysis as 从心，相聲. Its regular-script note describes the upper component 相 as 木 plus 目. This supports the traditional component account, not a specific pathway by which observing became thinking.
evidence.title: [A01403] 想 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.text: The supplied local Baxter–Sagart rows give 想 MC sjangX, OC *[s]aŋʔ, gloss ‘think’, and 相 reading 1 MC sjang, OC *[s]aŋ, gloss ‘mutually’; 相 reading 2 is MC sjangH, OC *[s]aŋ-s, ‘appearance, quality’. Same-system comparison of reading 1 with 想 is compatible with a phonetic relationship. Local rows are dataset evidence, not independent external evidence; Baxter–Sagart spellings should not be merged with Zhengzhang’s *slaŋʔ.
evidence.title: Old Chinese: A New Reconstruction

evidence.field: 相; 說文釋形與讀音
evidence.text: Records 相 as 从目从木 and gives its modern Mandarin readings xiàng and xiāng. The supplied exact local Unihan rows give 想 xiǎng and 相 xiāng; these current readings do not establish an ancient sound relationship. The official Unihan per-character endpoints were attempted but could not be opened during this research run.

search_audit.outcome: Search surfaced Xiaoxuetang’s form-evolution interface. Direct character-specific page and attempted rights-page access failed; no image URL was selected.

gaps: The reported late Spring and Autumn bronze form from 想簠 was not checked against an artifact catalogue, rubbing, or scholarly edition in this run. It remains a reported paleographic identification, not an inspected glyph; the inscription may be a vessel owner’s name or label rather than evidence for the common word ‘think’.

The transmitted *Chu Ci* citation is not a securely dated surviving graph witness. No first securely dated textual attestation or complete chronology of 想’s senses was established. Modern dictionary gloss order is not chronology.

The semantic route from 相 ‘look/observe’ to 想 ‘think/remember’ is not demonstrated by the inspected sources; the phonetic analysis does not require that semantic link. No evidence of graphic corruption was found.
No support was found for a whole-graph loan from 相 into 想. Sources describe 相 as the phonetic component within 想; no independent source-word/object borrowing account was established.

The supplied local exact rows were checked as provided: sources/unihan/Unihan_Readings.txt has 想 xiǎng and 相 xiāng; sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv has 想 MC sjangX / OC *[s]aŋʔ and two 相 readings, MC sjang / OC *[s]aŋ and MC sjangH / OC *[s]aŋ-s. The official per-character Unihan records were not successfully inspected, so the local rows are not externally verified here.

No historical glyph image was proposed. The Commons search did not establish an exact 想 file description page; Xiaoxuetang’s character-specific record and rights notice could not be inspected, so no exact glyph image URL and image reuse basis were verified.

limitations.text: No usable image candidate with verified exact identity and reuse provenance was established in this run. The ZDIC page reports bronze, *Shuowen* small-seal, and Eastern Han clerical forms, but its displayed images were not verified as direct reusable assets; the Xiaoxuetang record and rights notice could not be opened. No image is proposed.
